notes:
Summary: Coppergate Reserve is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical customer support and document search. Primary asks: firm throughput guarantees (target 400–500 reqs/s sustained with bursts to 1k), strict latency SLOs (p95 < 150 ms, p99 target < 200 ms ideally), reserved GPU planning for predictable unit economics (initial ask: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs with room to scale + burst pool), and enterprise-grade SLA language. They are cost-aware but willing to pay for stronger SLOs for higher-tier customers.

SLA specifics discussed: Redwood proposed 99.9% uptime for Dedicated with tiered credits. Coppergate counter: want 99.95% (monthly) for production routes serving paying customers; ask for clearer credit schedule with linear credits starting at 99.9 and more aggressive credit at <99.8. They requested contract examples showing credit calculations and a sample incident timeline.

Maintenance windows: prefer scheduled maintenance during 02:00–06:00 PT with minimum 72h notice, and opt-in to allow rolling upgrades during low-traffic windows. Coppergate wants a hard limit on emergency maintenance that requires 6h advance notice unless security-critical.

Support response times: Coppergate requires 24/7 support. P1 response target: 1 hour initial response and 4 hour remediation SLA for Dedicated, P2: 4 hour response, P3: next-business-day. Redwood initially offered 2 hour P1; SE working to escalate to 1 hour via premium support add-on.

Throughput & capacity planning notes: capacity planning spreadsheet shared (drive link). SE recommends starting with 8 reserved GPUs with autoscale burst pool of additional 4 GPUs for predictable headroom; proposed warm standby to reduce cold-start KV cache penalties. Ask: include commitment to maintain throughput for pinned model versions; require fallback policy to degrade to slightly larger-latency variant if capacity constrained.

Legal/security: Coppergate flagged data residency for EU customers; will require region pinning and audit log retention for 3 years. KMS integration required. SOC2 report and architecture diagram requested.

Quotes/paraphrase: "We need contractual certainty — if our SLAs are missed, the credit schedule must meaningfully offset customer refunds and cover our downstream SLAs." — Head of Platform (call 2026-03-08).
